title: Choose the visual world for GymShift
question: Cleaner home screen, phone first. The roll dealt Lane Lines. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Lane Lines
options.lineage: Painted gym-floor markings: turf sprint lanes, numbered zones, safety stencils on black rubber
options.thesis: Your shift is a painted lane: 3h finish line, hatched extension zone, and you move along it.
options.viewport: Header with first-name greeting; today's shift as a full-width lane with time markers, a yellow 'you are here' tick and the 3h–3h30 hatched extension zone; one huge yellow Clock out bar; location line; upcoming shifts as quiet numbered lanes.
options.risk: Black ground plus yellow can tip into hazard-sign alarm if yellow is used for anything but 'live'.

raised.raise: No greys doing status work: every state is either ink or ground, so nothing important fades.
Only the live shift is at full strength; every other shift steps back a full level.
One armature: spacing and lanes reflow in whole lane widths, never ad-hoc gaps.
Size ranks importance, so a reader with less English still sees what matters first.
Each state has one fixed mark that always travels with its plain word.

options.label: Next Service
options.lineage: Public-transport wayfinding and platform boards, built for readers of any language
options.thesis: Your next shift reads like the next train: one line, one time, one status word.
options.viewport: White ground; a black departure-board band for 'Now: Night shift 7:00 – 10:00 pm' with a status pill; a huge Clock out button; location as a pictogram line; upcoming shifts as a timetable list.
options.risk: The most familiar of these. Wayfinding is a well-worn app look, so it leans on craft rather than surprise.

options.label: Flat Tiles
options.lineage: Metro-style flat tiles and giant lowercase type
options.thesis: The words are the interface: giant lowercase 'clock out', flat colour tiles, no chrome.
options.viewport: Black ground; giant lowercase 'night shift' cropped at the edge; one big lime 'clock out' tile; small tiles for location and extension; upcoming shifts as a single tile column.
options.case: Holds clarity (big words, big targets) but nothing about it says gym or World Gym.
options.risk: Cropped giant type can hurt readers with less English, so cropping would be limited to decoration.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: Hours as a strobing black-and-white data field.
options.viewport: Clock state as a barcode field that inverts.
options.case: Loses both: dense monospace numbers fail readers with less English, and nobody on the team sees themselves in it.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: Shifts as poster tiles in horizontal rows.
options.viewport: Rows of shift tiles, focused one expands.
options.case: Loses both: horizontal rails hide upcoming shifts and turn a timesheet into browsing.
options.kept: Only the live item at full strength.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Times built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Giant grid-built 7:00 over faint graph lines.
options.case: Loses both: grid-built numerals read slower, and it says design school, not gym.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Shifts plotted as stars sized by importance.
options.case: Loses both: a metaphor to decode before you can clock in.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: State spoken in colour codes instead of words.
options.viewport: Colour strips that decode on hover.
options.case: Loses both: replacing words with codes is the opposite of what readers with less English need.
options.kept: One fixed mark per state, always with its word.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What shift-clock apps ship: white cards and a big round clock button, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, a shift card, a large circular Clock out button with a timer ring, then an upcoming list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every rostering app, and nothing ties it to World Gym.
